title: sys.exit(1) in library/context-manager code prevents caller recovery
detail: require_file/resolve_lora_path/GpuLock/run_session call sys.exit from non-entry modules. Raise exceptions instead; exit only in run.py entry point. The run_session context-manager site was NOT touched this run. Converting sys.exit to exceptions in library code is safe but ALWAYS breaks pre-existing tests that assert SystemExit (see gotcha:sysexit-to-exception-breaks-assert-tests).

title: subprocess.run/Popen calls lack timeout, returncode, and FileNotFoundError handling

NOTE: the audio facet introduced a regression — it SWALLOWED FileNotFoundError so the pre-existing test_audio_noise_detect.test_ffmpeg_not_found_propagates (expecting propagation) now fails (see gotcha:sysexit-to-exception-breaks-assert-tests — same root class: changing error semantics without updating the test that asserted the old semantics). detail: image-review.py:134: add_review_args() registers --output without checking whether it is already registered, creating a semantic conflict on the unified image parser. title: _arg_registered() helper inspects parser._actions — a CPython-private attribute that can break across argparse versions
detail: app/commands/_shared.py: the _arg_registered() / _option_registered() dedup-helpers iterate parser._actions to detect already-registered flags. parser._actions is a private attribute (leading underscore); CPython/argparse give no stability guarantee across versions, so the dedup logic that the entire unified-parser order-coupling pattern depends on is itself built on a fragile foundation. Run 2026-06-22T13-51-05 re-confirmed _shared.py:229 (_arg_registered/_option_registered iterate parser._actions — load-bearing foundation for every dedup guard, info). The load-bearing wall under the whole shared-flag skip architecture. Fix shape: prefer a parse_known_args probe or track registered dests in an explicit set rather than reaching into _actions.

title: A/B variation generate() reuses args.input_image / args.audio / ab_params across iterations — shared-state mutation yields correlated variants
detail: The A/B variation loop's generate() calls pass the SAME args.input_image / args.audio objects across iterations. Run 2026-06-22T00-32-25 APPLIED a partial config-layer fix (run_config.py ab_params now resolved via _resolve_ab_params). Fix shape: deep-copy or re-resolve per iteration; NEVER mutate args.* across variation iterations.

title: A module duplicates symbols from the live source module but is imported ONLY by tests — production and tests silently diverge
detail: app/commands/_output.py and app/commands/_model_resolver.py each re-implement symbols that already live in app/commands/_shared.py but are imported ONLY by their dedicated test files. Result: production code evolves in _shared.py while the test-only copy stays frozen — STRUCTURAL false-confidence trap (green tests do NOT mean live code works). Fix shape: delete the duplicate module and repoint test imports at the live source (_shared.py). Run 2026-06-21T17-06-24 APPLIED this (deleted _output.py + _model_resolver.py); grep for non-test importers before deleting.

title: Smoke tests run against the DEPRECATED ComfyUI/.venv produce spurious t2i/image/animate/generate failures; the correct venv is python/venv
detail: Any smoke failure mentioning ModuleNotFoundError / mlx / mflux is almost certainly a wrong-venv artifact, NOT a regression — re-run smoke with python/venv/bin/python before trusting a smoke failure. Run 2026-06-22T13-51-05 baseline: 15 smoke commands passed (main --help, t2i, image, refine, upscale, caption, replay, video, animate, import-lora-image, import-workflow, check-model, schema-defaults, generate, check-manifests); pytest 508 passed/0 failed baseline (python/venv). The task's hardcoded ComfyUI/.venv interpreter lacks mlx so python/venv was used. NOTE: this run's regressions (4 pytest failures) were NOT wrong-venv — they were genuine test-contract mismatches (see gotcha:sysexit-to-exception-breaks-assert-tests); always distinguish wrong-venv smoke noise from real pytest-contract failures.

title: del on a local rebound from getattr(self, name) deletes the local, not the instance attribute — dead op masquerading as cleanup
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-32-25 (FIX tier, seedvr2/pipeline.py unload): the cleanup loop bound `obj = getattr(self, name)` then `del obj` — but `del obj` only removes the local name binding, NOT the instance attribute, so the 'cleanup' silently did nothing (the attribute lived on). The correct form is `delattr(self, name)` (or `del self.__dict__[name]`). Common Python trap: re-assigning an attribute value to a local then deleting the local leaves the attribute untouched. Lint tools rarely flag it because the syntax is legal. Fix shape: iterate attribute names and call delattr(self, name) directly. Applied this run: replaced the dead `del obj` branch with `delattr(self, name)`.

title: A function annotated -> None that actually returns a value hides a real type/contract bug (mypy silently ignores the returned value)
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-32-25 (FIX tier, lora_utils.py _apply_lokr): _apply_lokr was annotated `-> None` but returns a tuple (module, metadata). A wrong return annotation is not merely cosmetic: in gradual typing, an explicit `-> None` annotation tells mypy the function has no meaningful return, so callers that consume the return value get flagged as the bug instead of the annotation. The mismatch also signals dead code or an incomplete refactor (someone added a return during a change but never updated the signature). Fix shape: when a function returns a value, annotate the real return type; when auditing a function, verify the annotation matches the actual return paths. Applied this run: corrected _apply_lokr to `-> tuple[nn.Module, dict[str, Any]]`.

title: Unused top-level imports accumulate monotonically as modules land without cleanup; the largest single dimension in full-scope scans
detail: Run 2026-06-22T12-34-52 surfaced 28 unused-top-level-import findings across ~28 files — the LARGEST dimension that run (28/60 = 47% of all findings). Recurring dead imports: top-level `import numpy as np` unused (all uses function-local re-imports, e.g. video_utils.py:13), `import sys`/`os`/`math`/`warnings`/`PIL.ImageFilter` unused, `field`/`timezone`/`datetime`/`dataclass`/`GenerationResult` unused, convert.py `import numpy as np` + `get_transformer_remapping` unused, redundant local re-imports shadowing module-level (image-i2i.py:892 `import numpy as _np` shadows `np`; import-checkpoint.py:24 `gc` shadowed by local re-import). The unused-import surface grows monotonically because new modules copy import headers from siblings and reviewers merge without pruning. Fix shape: prune unused imports on every PR; pyflakes (per MEMORY pyflakes-real-bug-hunting) is the reliable detector — filter f-string/unused-import noise, then the remainder is real. NOTE this run the import-hygiene lane also caught a REAL bug-class (run_config.py:176 local import binds resolve_lora_path which is never used in the function — not just cosmetic noise), so import-hygiene is NOT pure noise.

title: run_meta `or` falsy-coerce overrides explicit 0.0 AND misfires on empty list [] (list-typed multi-LoRA input) — doubly dangerous
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-32-25 (image-profile.py:530, correctness-image-profile-530, medium): run_meta's lora_scale is built via a falsy-coalesce (`val or default`) that silently overrides an explicit lora_scale=0.0 — the same `or`-overrides-zero family as mlx-review:or-pattern-overrides-zero, but with an extra twist: the input is list-typed (multi-LoRA action=append), so the coerce can ALSO misfire on an empty list [] (falsy) reverting to default when the user intended 'no LoRA scaling'. The list-typed variant is a NEW dimension of the falsy-coerce bug: booleans, 0, 0.0, '' AND [] are all falsy, so any list-typed argparse append field is vulnerable to the `or default` coerce when the user explicitly passes an empty list. Use explicit `if val is None: val = default` AND handle the empty-list case separately. This finding was NOT fixed this run (the list-typed input makes the safe fix non-trivial — need to distinguish [] (intentional no-LoRA) from None (unset)).

title: _run_single never lifts LTX events out of timings dict — events lost + timings polluted (single-run path diverges from A/B path)
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-11-42 (FIX tier, correctness-video-generate-891, HIGH): the SINGLE-run path _run_single in video-generate.py never pops 'events' out of the returned timings dict, so (a) LTX runtime events are silently lost (never surfaced to the Manifest.events capture added in commit 295d78e) and (b) the timings dict is polluted with a non-timing 'events' key. The A/B variation path (_run_variations) DID do this lift correctly — the single-run path had silently diverged from its sibling. Fix shape: mirror the A/B pattern — `_video_events = timings.pop('events', [])` then route _video_events to the manifest. APPLIED this run. GENERAL LESSON: when a feature (events capture) is added to one code path (A/B), audit the sibling path (single-run) for the same lift — divergence is silent because each path is tested in isolation.

title: Long-running network operations (CivitAI import, large safetensors download) have no retry — a single transient error kills a multi-GB import
detail: Run 2026-06-22T00-11-42 (error-handling-import-checkpoint-py-446, medium): the CivitAI API GET and the subsequent multi-GB safetensors download in import-checkpoint have NO retry — any transient network blip (TCP reset, 5xx, throttling) aborts an import that may have downloaded several GB, wasting the bandwidth and forcing a full restart. The same shape applies to import-lora-image. Fix shape: wrap the metadata GET in a short retry loop (3x backoff) and the binary download in a resumable/streaming fetch with Range support + retry on the chunk reader. Sibling class to mlx-review:subprocess-without-timeout (both are 'long op with no resilience to transient failure'). Distinct from that one because this is HTTP not subprocess, and the cost of failure is bandwidth-wasted not fd-leaked.

title: Magic-number seed default diverges from the project-wide default (42 vs 777) — silent wrong-seed at one call site
detail: Run 2026-06-22T12-34-52 (FIX tier, type-safety-image-faceswap-385, medium): image-faceswap.py:385 used getattr(args,'seed',42) — a magic-number default 42 that diverged from the project-wide default 777 (established as canonical per MEMORY zimage-cfg-wired-biggest-quality-lever). A user invoking faceswap WITHOUT setting --seed silently got seed=42 instead of 777, producing a different image than every other command. Fix shape: never hardcode a seed default; always getattr(args,'seed',777) or, better, use args.seed directly and let the parser's default=777 own the value. APPLIED this run: changed 42 -> 777. GENERAL LESSON: magic-number defaults are a silent-divergence trap — grep for getattr(args,'seed',<int>) and any literal != 777 is a bug. Sibling to the concrete-default-wins-cross-subaction family but localized to a single getattr call rather than a parser registration.

title: SeedVR2Upscaler.upscale had no MemoryError/RuntimeError handling (unlike ZImagePipeline) — heavy Metal-allocation path unguarded
detail: Run 2026-06-22T12-34-52 (FIX tier, error-handling-seedvr2-pipeline-204, medium): SeedVR2Upscaler.upscale (seedvr2/pipeline.py) wrapped its heavy Metal-allocation body (VAE encode -> denoise -> decode -> PIL conversion) with NO try/except, unlike ZImagePipeline.generate() which already had a MemoryError guard (added 2026-06-22T00-11-42). On Apple Silicon unified memory, the upscale path is a prime OOM site (decoding a large latent to full-res PIL). APPLIED this run: wrapped the heavy body in try/except (RuntimeError, MemoryError) with mx.clear_cache() flush + a clear M-series unified-memory message. GENERAL LESSON: every heavy-Metal-allocation path (encode/decode/upscale) needs the same MemoryError guard shape, not just the flagship generate() — audit all Pipeline.*.upscale / decode entry points when adding the guard to one.

title: motion_mean aliases flicker_mean — a derived metric masquerading as independent, so a 'has motion' gate never fires independently
detail: Run 2026-06-22T12-34-52 (correctness-video-t2i2v-300, medium): in video-t2i2v.py the motion_mean metric is computed as an ALIAS of flicker_mean (same underlying value), so any downstream gate like 'if motion_mean > threshold' is indistinguishable from the flicker gate — the 'has motion' check never fires independently of flicker. This is a correctness bug in the metric-definition layer: two semantically-distinct metrics (motion = frame-to-frame object displacement; flicker = frame-to-frame luminance variance) collapse to one number. Fix shape: compute motion_mean from optical-flow / pixel-displacement, not by aliasing the flicker metric. GENERAL LESSON: when adding a derived metric, verify it is computed from a DISTINCT signal, not aliased to a sibling metric — an alias silently makes every 'independent' gate redundant.

title: Converting sys.exit(1) -> raise Exception in library code breaks pre-existing tests that assert pytest.raises(SystemExit); FileNotFoundError-swallow breaks propagation-asserting tests
detail: Run 2026-06-22T13-51-05 (FIX tier) APPLIED the correct library-code fix (sys.exit -> exceptions per mlx-review:library-code-sys-exit) but ALL 4 regressions this run were test-CONTRACT mismatches, NOT source bugs: (1) replay.run() sys.exit(1)->exceptions broke test_video_dispatch.py::TestReplayRun (test_replay_missing_file / test_replay_bad_json / test_replay_unsupported_command) which assert pytest.raises(SystemExit) — they now see ValueError instead; (2) audio_noise_detect._extract_audio_pcm ffmpeg try/except FileNotFoundError swallow broke test_audio_noise_detect.py::TestExtractAudioPcm::test_ffmpeg_not_found_propagates which asserts the exception PROPAGATES — it now gets swallowed. The fix-change-logs listed only test_model_resolver.py + test_selftest_integrity.py as updated, MISSING these two test files. LESSON: whenever a fix changes error semantics (exception TYPE, or swallow-vs-propagate), grep the test suite for `pytest.raises(<old type>)` and `SystemExit`/`<old behavior>` at the same locus and update those tests IN THE SAME fix batch — otherwise pytest regresses and restore triggers. The restore correctly reverted ONLY the 2 test files while keeping all 19 source fixes (restore distinguishes test-contract drift from source regression). Fix shape: ALWAYS run grep -rn 'SystemExit|pytest.raises' app/tests/ before merging a sys.exit->exception fix, and include the touched test files in the fix's filesChanged list.

title: Streaming subprocess.Popen with `for line in proc.stdout` + proc.wait() blocks forever if the child hangs — replace with a deadline + communicate()
detail: Run 2026-06-22T13-51-05 (FIX tier, error-handling-image-purify-310, high): image-purify._run_transformer_backend streamed the child i2i run via `for line in proc.stdout` + `proc.wait()` with NO timeout — a hung child i2i run (OOM, Metal stall, deadlocked pipe buffer) blocks the parent forever, freezing the GUI job. APPLIED this run: replaced the unbounded streaming loop with a deadline-bounded communicate() pattern so a hung child is reaped after the timeout rather than blocking indefinitely. GENERAL LESSON: any `for line in proc.stdout` + `proc.wait()` streaming pattern is a latent deadlock (the pipe buffer can fill, the child can hang); prefer proc.communicate(timeout=...) or a select/poll loop with an explicit deadline. Sibling to mlx-review:subprocess-without-timeout but specifically the Popen-streaming deadlock facet (not the bare subprocess.run timeout).
